ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3 (effective Nov 1, 2024), 'Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information' (China); Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act Articles 7-11; Taiwan Countering Terrorism Financing Act; Taiwan Company Act Articles 387-1 and 387-4 requiring a register of substantial beneficial owners; and FSC AML/CFT rules for non-financial businesses.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Company Registration Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration Administration, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization exclusively: notarization by a Taiwan notary, followed by legalization by the competent consular office of the destination jurisdiction or the SEF/ARATS cross-strait mechanism for China; no Hague Apostille because Taiwan is not a contracting party to the Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Commercial Establishments Division, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization exclusively: notarization by a Taiwan notary, followed by legalization by the destination consular office or the SEF/ARATS cross-strait mechanism for China; no Hague Apostille is available for Taiwan-issued documents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors or sole shareholder of the WFOE's ultimate parent, if issued in an Apostille Contracting State
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille exclusively: obtain the apostille from the competent authority in the parent company's jurisdiction; do not add consular legalization. If the parent is in a non-member state, use consular legalization only. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) or the foreign registered agent/corporate service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization exclusively if issued by Taiwan authorities; if the certified copy is issued by a registered agent in an Apostille Contracting State, use Hague Apostille only. Never combine the two conventions in one chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank of the parent company (e.g., HSBC, DBS, or other qualifying bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only if the issuing bank is located in an Apostille Convention member state; consular legalization only if the issuing bank is located in a non-member state. The routes are strictly alternative and mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against OFAC SDN List, EU consolidated sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions lists, Taiwan FSC/MOJ domestic designations, and PBOC-sanctioned entities before appointing any director, shareholder, authorized signatory, or UBO. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification. Screening must include exact and fuzzy name matching, alias and date-of-birth cross-referencing, continuous monitoring, adverse media review, and red-flag indicators of corporate shell misuse. Findings must be escalated to the AML compliance officer and filed without tipping off the data subject.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company and Commercial Registration Online Portal - Company Name Pre-Approval (https://gcis.nat.gov.tw/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must be in Traditional Chinese. An English trade name may be registered and must correspond exactly through a four-tier naming convention: (1) local Chinese legal name, (2) English trade name, (3) romanized transliteration using Wade-Giles or Hanyu Pinyin, and (4) business descriptor aligned with ISIC/NAICS. The transliteration must not create a phonetically identical or misleading name with an existing registered company.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of receipt of the MOEA rejection notice, file a written administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs through the same portal, attaching the original rejection letter, a revised multi-tier transliteration plan, trademark search evidence, and legal grounds demonstrating that the proposed name is not prohibited, identical, or misleading. If the name contains a sensitive token, include any prior ministerial approval. The administrative appeal is automatically deemed granted if the MOEA fails to decide within the statutory appeal period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox can be used only for initial registration; however, the Taiwan National Taxation Bureau and commercial banks will normally reject a virtual-only address for uniform invoice registration and corporate bank account opening for a digital gaming company because of commercial substance requirements under Taiwan Company Act Articles 12 and 14 and the bank's AML customer due diligence policies. A physical local office with lease agreement, staff presence, telecommunications infrastructure, and visible signage is required, or the applicant will face denial of tax registration and Apple/Google payout account setup.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspection checklist: (1) verify registered signboard; (2) inspect hardware/software development equipment and server hosting agreements; (3) confirm staff attendance and payroll records; (4) review financial books and uniform invoice issuance; (5) interview the responsible person. The quantified risk for a cross-border-owned WFOE in the online gaming sector is approximately 15-20% during the first 12 months, increasing to 30% if the registered address is solely a virtual office or the company fails to maintain local records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, as amended, particularly Articles 18, 98-110, 128, 129, 161, 172, 193, 202, 208, 228, 230, 237, 387, and 393; Foreign Investment Act, particularly Articles 3, 8, and 10; and the Investment Commission Review Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan - Company Registration One-Stop Service Portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of Company under Article 387 of the Taiwan Company Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Taiwan Company Act imposes no minimum paid-in capital for limited liability companies. However, the subscribed capital must be actually paid in cash into a Taiwan bank account in the company name and verified by a Taiwan certified public accountant before the establishment registration is completed. The capital received from the foreign shareholder must match the amount approved by the Investment Commission. The funds are not permanently blocked after registration, but they must be held in a designated account until the CPA capital verification report is issued, and the inward remittance must be declared to the Central Bank of Taiwan.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Initial Capital Remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan - Online Investment Application System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before any Taiwan registry filing, the sole foreign shareholder must submit a foreign investment application under the Foreign Investment Act. The application must include identification documents, investment plan, capital remittance schedule, and proposed corporate name and business scope. The Investment Commission will review the proposal for restrictions under the negative list, national security, and capital control considerations. Upon approval, the investor receives a foreign investment approval certificate and an approved investment amount. The investor may then remit the initial capital into a Taiwan bank account held in the name of the future company, and the inward remittance must be declared to the Central Bank in accordance with the foreign exchange regulations. The capital must remain in the designated account until the post-incorporation capital verification report is issued by a Taiwan certified public accountant. Should any query be raised, the applicant must submit supplemental explanations within the official response period.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form
Certificate of incorporation of the investing entity
Passport or national identification of the beneficial owner
Draft Articles of Incorporation of the Taiwan company
Investment plan and capital remittance schedule
Power of attorney appointing the Taiwan local agent
Bank reference letter from the foreign shareholder's bank
Capital remittance declaration form after approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, submit the requested supplemental evidence through the online application system within the prescribed response period. If the application is rejected, the applicant may cure the stated defect and refile, or may file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days of the rejection decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Establishment Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan - Company and Commerce Registration One-Stop Service Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After foreign investment approval, reserve the company name and apply for establishment registration through the One-Stop Registration Portal. The applicant must log in, complete the application form, upload the articles of incorporation, the shareholder and director lists, the consent of the registered office address provider, and the foreign investment approval certificate. The application must be digitally signed using an approved electronic certificate, or the signatures must be notarized before a Taiwan notary public. The system will assess the official registration fee, and the applicant must pay electronically. The registry will examine the filing for legal compliance. If the documents are in order, the Department of Commercial Affairs will issue the establishment registration certificate and a uniform taxpayer identification number. It is essential that the registered business scope explicitly include online game software publishing and related information services.
required_dossiers: Company Name Reservation Certificate
Company Establishment Registration Application Form
Approved Articles of Incorporation
Foreign Investment Approval Certificate from the Investment Commission
List of directors and shareholders
Consent of the registered office address provider
Power of attorney or notarized authorization
CPA capital verification report and bank deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the establishment application is suspended or rejected for incomplete documents, the applicant must respond to the deficiency notice and resubmit the corrected filing through the One-Stop Portal. If the deadline is missed, withdraw and refile the application. The applicant may also submit an administrative petition to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days of a final rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Labor Insurance Registration, and Banking Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance; Bureau of Labor Insurance, Ministry of Labor; National Health Insurance Administration; Designated Foreign Exchange Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the establishment registration certificate is issued, apply for business tax registration at the local National Taxation Bureau to obtain the taxpayer identification certificate. In parallel, register as an employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and the National Health Insurance Administration so that statutory labor insurance and health insurance coverage are effective. Next, activate the permanent corporate bank account by presenting the incorporation certificate, taxpayer ID, company seal, and the board resolution. The bank will handle the Central Bank foreign exchange declaration for the capital remittance and may perform a beneficial ownership review. After activation, the company must maintain payroll, accounting, and statutory records. A corporate seal and responsible person seal must be created and registered with the appropriate agencies.
required_dossiers: Taiwan Company Establishment Registration Certificate
Taxpayer Identification Certificate Application Form
Company seal and responsible person seal
First Board Resolution authorizing bank account opening
Lease agreement or ownership documents for the registered office
Passports and residence certificates of the responsible persons
Labor insurance and health insurance registration forms
Board resolution appointing officers and signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is queried, provide the requested lease, financial, or ownership documents and request rectification. If the bank rejects the account opening application for compliance reasons, correct the beneficial ownership statement, supply additional board authorization, and resubmit. For labor insurance issues, amend employee data and refile the registration forms without termination of coverage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Corporate Governance Filings and Post-Establishment Administrative Matters
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs; Local National Taxation Bureau; Central Bank of Taiwan; Appointed Foreign Exchange Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt and execute the first board resolution, issue share certificates, and maintain the corporate minute book. Register the chairperson and directors with the Department of Commercial Affairs if the initial filing did not include the final appointments. If the inward capital remittance exceeds the approved foreign investment amount, file an investment amendment with the Investment Commission before spending the excess. For in-app purchase revenue from Apple and Google, register for electronic uniform invoices and cross-border transaction reporting with the tax authority, and arrange foreign exchange settlement through the appointed bank. The company should also appoint a registered agent in Taiwan, keep the registered office open during business hours, and preserve all board minutes, accounting ledgers, and statutory filings for a minimum of ten years.
required_dossiers: Executed First Board Resolution minutes
Share certificates issued to the sole shareholder
Directors and chairperson appointment form
Company seal registration form
Electronic uniform invoice registration form
Foreign exchange settlement and inward remittance forms
Registered office lease and service of process acknowledgment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a corporate filing is rejected, correct the record through the One-Stop Portal and pay any applicable late penalty. If the foreign exchange filing is rejected, coordinate with the designated bank to refile the remittance declaration. If the tax authority raises a query on the Apple or Google payouts, submit a reconciled cross-border transaction schedule and amend the electronic invoice registration accordingly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the business is digital MMORPG software publishing under ISIC 5820. No industrial manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing license is required from Taiwan industrial authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no statutory operating or manufacturing permit applies to pure digital software publishing. The company will operate under its general business registration and taxpayer identification certificate; voluntary digital content industry certifications may be sought for incentives only.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan, Taiwan
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category 5: No Environmental Impact Assessment is required because the project is a digital software publisher under ISIC 5820; it involves no factory construction, chemical process, mining, assembly, or warehousing operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero industrial process wastewater, zero VOC process emissions, and zero hazardous waste generation. General office waste must be collected through licensed municipal waste services under the Waste Disposal Act. If the leased office undergoes fit-out, the building occupancy permit and fire safety chapters of the Building Act must be observed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for an industrial civil-defense manufacturing or warehouse permit. For the leased commercial office, obtain the Fire Safety Equipment Inspection Certificate and formulate a fire safety management plan as required by the Fire Services Act. No structural load certification is required for a software publishing office beyond the landlord's building occupancy certificate, and the company must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act for routine workplace safety and fire drills.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), administered through the Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax) online portal at www.chinatax.gov.cn; local tax filing is under the STA branch at the WFOE's statutory incorporation address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) incorporated in mainland China, the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) serves as the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number; no separate TIN application is required. The WFOE must then complete taxpayer registration information through the STA e-Tax portal, file for VAT General Taxpayer status where annual turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000 or on an elective basis, and complete export tax refund/zero-rating registration if it intends to export services or goods. A foreign non-resident entity (including a Taiwan-resident parent) that has no PRC permanent establishment must separately complete Non-Resident Enterprise Tax Registration through the STA e-Tax system; the STA assigns a non-resident Tax Identification Number used for Chinese withholding obligations (dividends, royalties, service fees). The Taiwan-resident parent must provide a certificate of its foreign tax identification and, where applicable, a Certificate of Residence for treaty benefits before any PRC withholding is computed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The People's Republic of China does not provide a check-the-box election, partnership pass-through election, or hybrid entity classification election for a WFOE. Enterprise Income Tax is levied on the entity as a resident taxpayer on worldwide income; controlled foreign corporation and hybrid mismatch anti-avoidance rules apply mandatorily. VAT General Taxpayer versus Small-Scale Taxpayer is only an indirect-tax collection status, not an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 0 - a mainland China-incorporated WFOE must register for VAT upon commencement of taxable activity; RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable turnover is the statutory threshold above which VAT General Taxpayer registration is mandatory, and below which Small-Scale Taxpayer status applies unless the WFOE elects General Taxpayer status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices (including Special VAT Invoices and digital VAT invoices) must be issued through the STA-approved e-Invoice Service integrated with the Golden Tax System Phase IV. Invoice data are encrypted, assigned a unique tax invoice code, and transmitted to the STA in real time before the counterparty may claim input VAT credit. B2B purchasers cannot deduct input VAT without an STA-cleared electronic invoice matching the transaction. Export zero-rated sales must be invoiced through the same e-Invoice platform using the export sales tariff code and supporting export documentation; unregistered offline invoicing is prohibited.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For physical software carriers sold overseas, 0% VAT applies to goods exported from mainland China where a customs export declaration is accepted and export proceeds are repatriated in foreign currency. For digital delivery of the MMORPG and in-app purchases through Apple App Store and Google Play, zero-rating is available where the services or digital content are supplied to customers outside mainland China, are wholly consumed outside the customs territory, are paid for with foreign currency, and are supported by platform payout documentation. The WFOE must demonstrate that the sale is an export of services rather than a domestic supply; absence of an overseas end-customer or foreign-currency consideration will reclassify the supply as taxable at the applicable domestic VAT rate. Pure digital transactions do not require customs clearance, but the exporter must retain platform sales/payout evidence and cross-border bank receipts.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) - export goods customs declaration for physical software carriers, with the customs office endorsement and unique customs declaration number; not applicable to pure digital downloads
Bill of Lading or airway waybill - evidencing physical delivery of exported goods to the overseas consignee; omitted where the export is purely digital

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) - or, where the foreign exchange administration requires it, the bank-issued Cross-Border Receipts Declaration - evidencing repatriation and settlement of foreign-currency consideration through a Chinese bank
Export contract or online distribution agreement with Apple App Store and Google Play showing overseas territories, user market, and revenue-sharing mechanism
Apple App Store and Google Play payout statements and financial dashboard reports for the tax period, reconciling gross sales, platform commissions, and net remittance to the WFOE
Software copyright registration certificate or intellectual property ownership/royalty documentation (supplementary evidence for intangible export treatment)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA may audit export zero-rating applications through the Golden Tax System cross-matching customs, foreign exchange, invoice, and platform payment data. If documentation is incomplete, the sale is consumed in mainland China, or foreign-currency receipts are not repatriated within 180 days, the WFOE loses zero-rating and must output VAT at the applicable domestic rate (13% or, for qualifying electronic services, 6%), plus daily late-payment surcharges of 0.05% of the unpaid tax and an administrative penalty ranging from 50% to five times the tax underpaid under the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection. Serious cases involving fabricated documents or false export refund claims are subject to criminal prosecution for defrauding export tax rebates under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, with fines and imprisonment, confiscation of the fraudulently obtained refund, and mandatory reversal of any input VAT previously credited.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan), acting through its Foreign Exchange Administration, under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act and supervised through Authorized Foreign Exchange Banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan operates a managed-float foreign exchange regime with liberalised current-account convertibility and regulated capital-account convertibility. The Taiwan WFOE will be permitted to receive payments for digital game publishing, settle royalties, hold foreign-currency deposits, and convert New Taiwan dollars at market rates through Authorized Banks without a bureaucratic exchange allocation mechanism. However, the capital account is not fully open: inbound equity contributions for the WFOE must be approved by the competent foreign-investment authority and matched against the approved investment amount before conversion into TWD. Export receipts, including app-store proceeds from Apple and Google, are treated as service export earnings and must be evidenced by platform payout statements, underlying contracts, and proper foreign-exchange declarations; there is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio. Profit remittance to overseas shareholders is feasible after delivering audited financial statements, tax payment confirmation, corporate board resolutions, and documentary proof of the underlying distributed profit, with the primary obstacle being evidentiary completeness rather than rationing. For an ISIC 5820 hardcore MMORPG global operation, the key convertibility sensitivity lies in proving that income from Taiwan-source players is properly separated from cross-border software sales and that royalties paid to the mainland China parent or related technology licensor are at arm's length. The Central Bank requires each settlement to be classified under the correct current-account or capital-account purpose code, and banks will reject unsupported FX transactions that resemble round-tripping, fake cross-strait trade, or unapproved financing. Overall, the regime is workable for a professionally structured WFOE, but capital injections, shareholder loans, and any TWD hedging transactions must be pre-documented and filed with the Authorized Bank before execution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan does not impose a statutory percentage surrender requirement for export proceeds. Export foreign-currency receipts may be retained in foreign-currency deposit accounts at Authorized Banks, but they must be declared and settled through the bank in accordance with the underlying trade or service contract, normally within the agreed credit term, commonly under 180 days from invoice or service completion. For digital game publishing revenue received from Apple App Store and Google Play, the WFOE must maintain the platform payout statement, merchant agreement, and tax invoice to demonstrate service export character; conversion into TWD is optional and executed at the prevailing market rate once the bank has recorded the foreign-exchange declaration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Multi-Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Mega International Commercial Bank Co., Ltd.
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational TWD Account, USD/CNY Foreign Currency Account, and Investment Settlement Ledger
Corporate Checking Account, USD Concentration Account, and App-Store Payout Settlement Account
Foreign Currency Deposit Account and New Taiwan Dollar Operating Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally unsuitable as the primary treasury spine. Taiwan's Foreign Exchange Regulation Act confines foreign-exchange dealing, FX deposit-taking, trade settlement declaration, and remittance reporting to Authorized Banks supervised by the Central Bank. Offshore digital EMIs are not licensed Authorized Banks for Taiwan domestic FX purposes, cannot hold the WFOE's statutory capital escrow, cannot issue capital verification certificates, and cannot lawfully convert TWD or process Taiwan-source export settlement. A fintech EMI may be used only as an auxiliary collection wallet in a foreign jurisdiction for non-Taiwan ancillary transactions, but it must not be used for capital subscription, dividend remittance, statutory audit confirmation, or the main USD payouts coming from Apple and Google. The recommended solution is to route all material inbound and outbound FX through Bank of Taiwan or Mega International Commercial Bank, reserving the fintech layer strictly for small operational payments outside Taiwan where such EMI services are locally permitted.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is effectively mandatory for the statutory directors or the authorized Taiwanese resident manager when opening the WFOE's first corporate bank account. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted by Taiwan Authorized Banks as a complete substitute because the institution must complete a real-person interview with the ultimate beneficial owner or senior managing official under local AML rules. In practice, Bank of Taiwan and Mega will require the chairperson or a designated director to attend in person, present the original passport, company registration, organizational certificate, and company seal charter, and answer questions regarding the ultimate beneficial owner chain. A notarized and legalized power of attorney may allow a local finance manager to execute account operation documents after the principal passes the initial interview, but it will not waive the bank's right to interview the beneficial owner, particularly when the shareholder chain is cross-strait and involves a mainland China parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner opacity through a mainland China corporate shareholder chain, where the Taiwan WFOE is owned by a Hong Kong or mainland intermediate and the natural-person shareholders are not visible from public registries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the complete group organogram from Taiwan WFOE up to every natural-person UBO with a 25% or greater interest, notarized certificates of incorporation and registers of members for all intermediate Hong Kong or offshore holding companies, three years of audited parent-company financial statements, source-of-wealth records for each capital injection, bank reference letters from the parent's principal banks, external World-Check / LexisNexis screening reports, and a sworn statement from the Taiwan statutory director explaining the commercial rationale for the multilayer structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume Apple App Store and Google Play microtransaction flows being misinterpreted as unvetted consumer deposits, gambling-like receipts, money laundering, or unreported Taiwan-source taxable revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the executed Apple Developer Program and Google Play Developer distribution agreements, merchant-of-record contracts, consolidated platform payout reports covering a minimum of twelve months, transaction-level anonymized revenue analytics by geographic region, CPA-issued foreign service revenue reconciliation, the Taiwan WFOE's gaming license or regulatory registration statement if applicable, and a written narrative distinguishing in-app purchase revenue from prohibited gambling or money-laundering activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicion of trade-based money laundering via intercompany royalty, licensing, or marketing-service payments from the Taiwan WFOE to mainland China affiliates, especially when intangible digital-goods valuations are difficult to verify.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit arm's-length intercompany service and intellectual property license agreements, a full transfer pricing study covering the WFOE's profitability and royalty rates, underlying tax invoices and contracts for each payment, hosting and server agreements, screenshots or contractual evidence of actual game development services, Taiwan tax clearance certificates, and confirmation that each outward remittance has a matching current-account transaction declaration with the Authorized Bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions, political-exposure, or state-associated capital exposure if the mainland parent or any beneficial owner appears in public procurement records, sanctioned-company databases, or negative media related to cross-strait investment restrictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide current sanctions and PEP screening reports for all directors, shareholders owning 25% or more, and the authorized banking signatories; global negative-media search results; a state-ownership attestation signed by the UBO; if any sovereign wealth fund or state-connected investor is present, a defensive memorandum from Taiwanese counsel confirming the investment did not violate the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals and a regulatory comfort letter if available.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan WFOE must first obtain the investment approval from the competent foreign-investment authority before receiving equity capital. Once approved, the parent should instruct its remitting bank to issue a SWIFT MT103 to the Authorized Bank in Taiwan under the foreign-exchange purpose code for foreign investment equity contribution, with the parent company's name, WFOE name, and approval-number reference stated in the remittance narrative. The Taiwan bank will book the inward remittance into a foreign-currency investment escrow account, file the statutory inward declaration with the Central Bank, and convert to TWD only after matching the remittance to the approved investment amount. Within the prescribed period after receipt, the WFOE must appoint a Taiwan CPA to issue a capital verification report confirming that the funds have been paid in and booked to paid-in capital. Shareholder loans must be processed under a separate capital-account purpose code and should never be commingled with equity injection; all subsequent transfers from the escrow ledger into the operating currency account must be made through clearly documented internal treasury entries and retained for the bank's supervision audit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For worldwide MMORPG operational disbursements, SWIFT MT103 is the primary clearing rail for intercompany royalty payments, third-party software development fees, legal and tax advisory invoices, and tax withholdings. Commercial Letters of Credit and Documentary Collections should be reserved for physical-goods scenarios such as licensed merchandise, console accessory shipments, or hardware co-development deliveries subject to transport documents; they are not necessary for purely digital app-store transactions. Apple App Store and Google Play proceeds will normally enter the Taiwan WFOE as aggregate USD wires from Apple or Google payment intermediaries; the treasury must match each wire to the corresponding platform payout statement, reconcile against the foreign-service export invoice, and only then convert net balances to TWD through the Authorized Bank. All outward remittances must carry the correct Central Bank purpose classification, underlying agreement reference, invoice, tax withholding evidence if applicable, and the beneficiary's banking details, ensuring the clearing path remains transparent for both local tax filing and upstream AML reviews.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward contracts with a Taiwan domestic Authorized Bank for genuine TWD/USD and TWD/CNY exposures arising from known app-store payout schedules and intercompany royalty payments, with tenors matched to the underlying current-account invoices and approved trade documentation.

Cross-currency swaps limited to documented intercompany receivables and payables for actual MMORPG licensing and game-development transactions, executed only with Authorized Banks and supported by the underlying contracts, invoices, and Central Bank declaration records.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally not suitable for the onshore Taiwan WFOE and should not be booked domestically without Central Bank approval; NDFs may be considered only by the offshore parent entity hedging Taiwan-related exposure outside Taiwan.

FX options with simple premium structures may be used selectively by the treasury to hedge uncertain app-store revenue conversion, provided they are documented as genuine risk-management instruments and the bank classifies them under the permitted derivatives scope for corporate hedge execution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder approval of audited financial statements (annual general meeting for a company limited by shares; unanimous shareholder consent for a limited company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of record; resolution and attendance records entered in the statutory Minute Book; approved statements then filed with MOEA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (by June 30 for calendar-year entities); extension requires MOEA approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible directors exposed to fines of NT$10,000–50,000 and damages to shareholders; MOEA may order convening and, for habitual default, administrative dissolution under Company Act Article 10

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of approved annual financial statements, business report, and profit appropriation or loss-covering resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce (經濟部商業司)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after shareholder approval (typically by July 15 for calendar-year filers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of NT$10,000–50,000 per responsible person for non-filing or untrue particulars; the entity's registry record is marked for non-compliance and may be subject to dissolution order

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual substantial shareholder and responsible person report (Company Act Article 22-1 electronic filing) covering directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding more than 10% of shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA Company Registration Information System (公司申報與查詢平台)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By June 30 of each year, reporting data as of December 31 of the preceding fiscal year; any mid-year change must be re-filed within 15 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of NT$500,000–5,000,000 (approx. USD 16,000–165,000) per violation with recurring fines until rectified; serves as the annual legal confirmation of shareholding transfers and officer changes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax final return and profit-seeking enterprise tax payment (營利事業所得稅結算申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (財政部各地區國稅局)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By May 31 of the year following the calendar tax year; electronic filing extension calendar published by the taxation bureau applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of 1% of the deficiency for every 2 days, capped at 15%, plus daily interest; late return filed before investigation triggers a 10% delinquency surcharge; non-filing triggers estimated assessment with penalty up to 3x of under-assessed tax and compulsory collection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding and non-withholding income statements for salaries, director remuneration, dividends, and royalties (各類所得扣繳暨免扣繳憑單申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (各地區國稅局)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By January 31 of the year following the payment year; employee copies of the withholding statements delivered by the same date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under-withholding penalty up to 100% of the short-withheld amount; late or omitted filing of statements subject to fines up to NT$100,000 plus daily interest on any short-paid tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested enterprise annual operational report (僑外投資事業年度經營狀況申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA Department of Investment Review (經濟部投資審議司)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 following the reporting year, per the Investment Commission's annual circular
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Compliance warning for late or incomplete returns; repeated non-compliance is recorded in the investment review file and may impair future foreign investment applications or support revocation of investment approval

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory CPA audit of the annual financial statements when paid-in capital equals or exceeds NT$30 million (approx. USD 1.0 million) or when annual net turnover equals or exceeds NT$100 million (approx. USD 3.3 million) under Company Act Article 20 and MOEA thresholds; the tax authority likewise requires CPA-attested return attachments above the revenue threshold. Below these thresholds, a CPA review or compilation is sufficient absent special regulatory requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-public companies apply the Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standard (企業會計準則公報, EAS), converged with IFRS for SMEs; publicly traded companies apply TIFRS (IFRS as endorsed by the FSC). A foreign-owned subsidiary consolidating under IFRS may apply full IFRS at the statutory level with MOEA approval.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: By June 30 of each year, the company must electronically confirm to MOEA the register of directors, supervisors, managers, and all shareholders holding more than 10% of the shares, using data as of the preceding December 31; any share transfer or officer change during the year must be re-filed within 15 days. Concurrently, the AML beneficial-ownership record (實質受益人資料) maintained at the registered office must be kept current and be available for inspection by MOEA or FSC examiners; no notarization is required for a standard low-risk private company.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Supervisors (董事及監察人名冊)
Shareholders' Meeting Minute Book (股東會議事錄)
Articles of Incorporation and all amendments (公司章程及歷次修正條文)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600–2,000 per year for a Taipei registered office and corporate secretarial agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000–30,000 per year for a cross-border digital services company with global MMORPG revenue requiring an EAS/IFRS-compliant CPA audit

stage_6.line_or_box_code: Form 15 — Cover Page Box 1 (公司基本資料)
stage_6.entry_description: Unified Business Number (統一編號), registered name, industry code (sw. TW industry code 5820-software publishing), paid-in capital, fiscal year period.
